query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a hierarchical microstructure with a grain size optimized between 2-5 μm and a bimodal grain distribution will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys by enhancing strain hardening and reducing microcracking.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries
generation.intervention: Designing a hierarchical microstructure with optimized grain size and distribution
generation.mechanism: Tailoring microstructure to optimize grain size, shape, and distribution, which enhances strength and ductility by reducing microcracking and improving strain hardening. This is achieved by creating a bimodal grain distribution that combines the benefits of fine grains (high strength) and coarse grains (high ductility), as supported by prior research on grain size effects in high-entropy alloys [no specific records provided].
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in yield strength (from 800 MPa to 960 MPa) and a 30% increase in tensile ductility (from 10% to 13%) relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, which is comparable to or exceeds existing state-of-the-art values for eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.boundary: Grain size range: 2-5 μm, grain distribution: bimodal, with a ratio of fine to coarse grains between 1:1 and 1:3, which directly influences the mechanism by optimizing the balance between strength and ductility.
generation.uncertainty: The actual optimal grain size and distribution may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions. Further research is needed to fully understand the effects of hierarchical microstructure on the mechanical properties of eutectic high-entropy alloys.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of hierarchical microstructure samples with varying grain sizes and distributions, compared to a control experiment using unmodified lamellar-colony samples. The control experiment will use identical sample preparation and testing conditions to ensure a fair comparison.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength and tensile ductility of the hierarchical microstructure samples do not exceed the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline by at least 18% and 22%, respectively, the hypothesis is falsified.
